title: Declare the batch schema and refuse malformed batches
problem: Drift statistics computed over a malformed batch look exactly like drift. A missing column, a unit change or a string in a numeric field will move every distribution, and the monitor will report a model problem that is really a pipeline problem.
context: This is the first task of a learner-authored forge project. No source exists yet. The learner creates the repository, chooses its structure, and owns every design decision inside the specification's constraints.
impact: Every later statistic assumes the batch is well formed. If malformed data can reach the drift computation, the monitor cannot tell a pipeline fault from real drift.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The reference window and live batches share a schema declared as data: columns, types and allowed domains, plus the prediction column and a batch identity.
A batch with a missing or extra column, a wrong type, or out-of-domain values is refused. The error names the column and the first offending rows.
Each batch has an identity, and resubmitting the same batch is detected.
A synthetic batch generator produces reference and live batches from a seed, so every later test is reproducible.
Automated tests cover a valid batch and at least three distinct malformed ones, plus a duplicate submission, and pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains the schema choices, one rejected alternative, and what breaks first if an upstream system silently changes a unit.

constraints: Standard library plus a test runner only. No dataframe or schema library for this task.
No network access and no model API. Every input is synthetic and generated or checked in by the learner.
Do not compute drift or performance yet. This task ends at validated, identified batches.
Do not push to a remote or open a pull request as part of this task.

scope.description: One input boundary, its validation, identity and a reproducible generator.

investigation_areas: Which malformations would look like drift if they reached the statistics
What identifies a batch so a duplicate is caught
How a seeded generator makes every later result reproducible
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design; the learner chooses the runner and the layout.
documentation_requirements: Record the schema, the batch identity scheme and the rejected alternative in the learner design.
